title: Machine learning outperforms Padua and IMPROVE scores for hospital-acquired VTE
summary: On 379,720 MIMIC-IV admissions (674 with imaging-confirmed VTE) out-of-fold AUCs were 0.79 to 0.81, against 0.707 for Padua and 0.688 for IMPROVE. Frozen models in 29,144 Beijing admissions did better than both scores, with the admission-safe model at AUC 0.706 versus 0.678. Discrimination is modest, and the authors call for recalibration and prospective validation; this is a retrospective preprint.
ai_technology: XGBoost and logistic regression models on EHR data
organization: Department of Hematology, Peking Union Medical College Hospital, Beijing, China

evidence.tested: External validation of frozen models in a separate tertiary hospital in Beijing.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance and effect on prophylaxis decisions; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models predicted imaging-confirmed in-hospital VTE.
